newsitem.title: UK: P&O confident Stena JV to go ahead.
newsitem.headline: P&O confident Stena JV to go ahead.

text.p: Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Co said on Thursday it was "still confident" its proposed joint venture with Stena Line AB of Sweden would go ahead despite reports of European Commission doubts over the deal.
"We are not expecting any major delay," a P & O spokesman told Reuters.

The spokesman was responding to reports that the Commission's competition service has drafted a "letter of serious doubts" about the deal, which would merge the two company's ferry operations in the English channel.
He said the company has already held a series of talks with the Commission over the proposed merger and pointed out that the letter has not yet been sent.

The final decision to send the letter -- there is a June 11 deadline -- must be taken by European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert in consultation with his transport counterpart Neil Kinnock and the Commission's legal service, according to a European Union source in Brussels.
On Monday, the French authorities gave their approval to the deal -- one of the three authorities which have to sanction the proposed joint venture.

The P & O spokesman said UK trade and industry secretary Margaret Beckett is expected to publish the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) report on the deal "later next week or early the following week".
The MMC report was completed on April 4 but publication was delayed by the UK general election.

The deal would create a new company controlled equally by the two groups, but with Stena owning 40 percent and P & O 60 percent, with total assets amounting to around 410 million pounds ($669 million). It would operate the Dover-Calais, Dover-Zeebrugge and Newhaven-Dieppe routes.
